entry.title: Securely Connect to a Remote PostgreSQL Database with SSH Tunneling
entry.summary:
Securely Connect to a Remote PostgreSQL Database with SSH Tunneling
Exposing your database port directly to the internet is like leaving your house unlocked with a “welcome” sign on the door. A safer approach is to use an SSH tunnel (a secure pipe between your local machine and the remote server). This way PostgreSQL can stay bound to localhost on the server, while you still connect from your laptop. If you don’t already have an SSH key, generate one locally: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Private key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
Public key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
Keep the private key safe and never share it. The public key is what you’ll add to the server. Replace user@remote-server.com with your real username and server address: ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub user@re…
